cues: The story has two halves of opposite mood.
In the first, festive and comic, the narrator echoes the neighbours' admiration.
After the hinge, the narrator moves close to Varma and even borrows his words, calling Veena a smiling, hypocritical pudding.
And we are never once taken inside Rakesh's mind.
That is why the ending lands like an accusation: we know what the father feels, and can only guess at the son.
